items.statement: Determine whether and how the three supplied molecules differ in low-energy singlet absorption and in the spatial character of the associated electronic excitations in dichloromethane. Develop and test a molecular explanation for any established differences, or establish a defensible limit on what can be distinguished. Assess what the evidence supports about the relation between molecular structure and these excitation properties. No spectral ordering or state assignment is supplied.
items.expected: Answer what low-energy optical or excitation-character differences are supported within the three-molecule DCM scope, how strongly the molecular explanation is supported, and what remains unresolved. Accept supported reverse order, revised state assignments, negative findings and bounded non-identifiability. Do not require all states to be CT, the source assignments, a fixed torsion effect or a unique mechanism. Missing calculations are not negative evidence, and vertical monomer results alone do not explain fluorescence yield, aggregate/solid-state emission or device behavior.
